note: Real-ELF ProgramTest for the canonical Rational Representation V2 waist -- open-market structured issuance/unwrap/denominate/reconstitute plus terminal redemption (blocked.json: 'A real-ELF ProgramTest for this route already exists and passes; it simply does not emit census evidence yet'). Real Claims, Custody, Registry and Core ELFs plus the genuine, canonically-built Token-2022 v11 runtime, with the Product graph and LiabilityBasisV2 aggregate INSTALLED directly. Campaign: programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/tests/rational_representation_v2_program_test.rs. Every submitted transaction goes through a test-only wrapper that CPIs into Claims, so a refusal Claims itself raises propagates the same numeric code to the wrapper's own top-level failure log -- a failed CPI aborts the whole transaction before the wrapper's Rust code regains control, so that repetition is the runtime's own account of the failure depth, not a second refusal.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: create the Claims-role Custody replay
bindings.note: The Claims-role Custody replay this Market's redemption needs, CREATED rather than planted. Claims forwards a Custody InitializeReplay under its own release-pinned caller authority; Custody creates the account at the role-seeded replay PDA (decision 0008 section 7). Every terminal case in this campaign now opens with this transaction, so the redemption below consumes the cursor the chain actually wrote -- revision 1, zero open Vaults -- instead of one the fixture invented. 711 legacy bytes against the 1,232 limit, asserted: creating this cursor must not require a published lookup table.

The winning terminal redemption refuses Identity (0x5002) and the campaign asserts the Hoard and the recipient are byte-identical. Custody would refuse it a layer down on ReplayBindingMismatch; the point is that Claims does not get there.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: recipe substitution: permuted coefficients
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A same-width RepresentationDescriptorV2 whose coefficients are the canonical ones PERMUTED -- a valid record naming a recipe the composition does not state. Built by mutating the DERIVED preimage, so it is a near-miss of the real record rather than a hand-written seventh one. Refused twice for two reasons: host-side, require_coefficients_are_the_composition_root will not mint it (the join the live route lost when authenticate_exposure replaced authenticate_graph, decision 0011 s3d); on chain, Identity (0x5002) because the request names a descriptor_id that is the digest of other bytes.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: receipt backed by receipt
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the campaign records WHERE it dies rather than claiming Claims caught it. Coordinate zero's asset row and account frame name the RECEIPT Mint, so a receipt would be backed by itself. RepresentationRequestV2::decode refuses those bytes outright (AccountAlias), and EVERY caller must decode the request to derive its own Trading authority (CallerAuthoritySeedsV1 over the request's parent_context) -- so the request can never acquire a signer and never reaches the Claims CPI at all. The test-only wrapper refuses at its own Instruction code (0x104000) at 11,302 CU. The founding-time half is proved separately in the same test: StructuredTermsV2::bind_shard_terms refuses a receipt Mint aliasing a shard Mint with DuplicateIdentity.

unnamed_refusal.reason: RationalV2CallerError::Instruction, raised by the campaign's TEST-ONLY wrapper program, not by a first-party dClutch program. That is the honest depth: the wrapper decodes the request to derive its Trading caller authority exactly as a real caller must, so a request the grammar rejects can never acquire a signer and can never reach the Claims CPI. Recorded as unnamed because the wrapper's refusal band is test scaffolding and must not enter any program's taxonomy.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: one-atom K_i skew at coordinate 0
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Coordinate 0's backing skewed by exactly ONE shard atom. The callee recomputes K_i = S * c_i as asset.coefficient * header.quantity (plan.rs:263) and the campaign basis [2, 3, 5] over 7 is pairwise coprime and coprime to the denominator precisely so a one-atom skew at one coordinate cannot be presented as a legitimate quantity at another. Refuses Representation (0x5008) at 313,356 CU.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: the winning terminal redemption replayed
bindings.note: HOSTILE, double redeem. The identical winning redemption resubmitted at a LATER SLOT, so it carries a different blockhash and a different signature and the runtime's duplicate-signature dedup is not what stops it. Claims itself refuses Identity (0x5002) at 181,418 CU, having already consumed the representation replay's revision and the Custody replay's cursor; the settled state stays byte-identical.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: issue against a receipt Mint with only the Mint role
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and it CORRECTS decision 0011 s3b. The receipt Mint carries the representation authority as its Mint authority and NOT as its permissioned-burn authority: s3b's under-configured founding, which the ruling predicted would let Issue commit and then fail at BurnReceipt 'at the Token program with the descriptor already committed'. Measured: parse_behavior_mint reads the receipt Mint's Token-2022 behavior profile on every action and requires the permissioned-burn authority present and pinned, so the FIRST IssueStructured refuses Token (0x5009) at 255,972 CU with ZERO Token-2022 CPIs issued. The two-role cost is real; its consequence is a founding that can never issue, not a representation that can never be unwound.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: unwrap against a receipt Mint with only the Mint role
bindings.note: The consequence of the row above, recorded for what it is rather than for what it looks like: the Issue committed nothing, so no representation replay exists to carry revision one and the unwrap is refused on Accounts (0x5001) at 251,184 CU. BurnReceipt is never the thing that fails, because there is never anything to unwrap.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: a wallet-held Position is paid
bindings.note: STEP TWO OF THE REDEMPTION, and the first execution this route has ever had. A PLAIN WALLET signs for its own Position under the widened execution role Claims (decision 0008 s8): coordinate 0 carries the owner's signature instead of a caller-program PDA, and because a program-derived address has no key, that signature IS the proof the Position is wallet-held. 354,370 CU. Hoard 9 -> 7 and recipient 5 -> 7 for the two claims the wallet held at the winning coordinate; the Position's winning balance is burned to zero, the aggregate's supply falls by the same atoms, no other coordinate moves, both revisions advance by one and the Claims-role cursor advances from the value InitializeReplay wrote. The representation layer -- shard Mints, capability Positions -- is byte-identical.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: the Position owner pays its own fee
bindings.note: THE BROWSER'S SHAPE. One wallet pays the fee AND authorizes, so coordinate 0 arrives WRITABLE: an account that is both a fee payer and a readonly signer compiles to a single writable-signer entry, and there is no message in which one wallet can present itself readonly. Decision 0008 s8.4 relaxes the frame spec's readonly pin for role Claims along that one axis only. 354,369 CU -- one unit under the two-signer shape, which is the whole cost of the difference.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: a losing wallet coordinate pays zero
bindings.note: terminal_settlement_v3's ZERO-PAYOUT BRANCH, which nothing in the tree had ever executed. 223,244 CU. The wallet's claim at a losing coordinate is burned and the aggregate's supply falls -- a worthless claim is still a claim, and retiring it is a real transition -- but Custody is never invoked (no 'Program <custody> success' in the logs), the Hoard and the recipient are byte-identical afterwards, and the Claims-role cursor does not move. authenticate_zero_custody_accounts is what re-derives the whole Custody frame from the persisted namespace without spending it.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: the first half of a wallet payout
bindings.note: A PARTIAL redemption: one of the wallet's two winning claims, 354,370 CU. Exists to set up the stale-cursor row below, and to record that quantity is a caller coordinate the evaluator bounds against the Position's own balance rather than a whole-position sweep.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: a wallet payout on a stale Custody cursor
bindings.note: HOSTILE, the double-spend shape. The second payout names the revisions the first left behind, so the aggregate and the Position join cleanly, and carries the STALE Custody cursor. Refused Identity (0x5002) at 226,195 CU, and the honest depth is that CLAIMS refuses it, not Custody: authenticate_custody_accounts reads the replay's own next_revision and compares it to the request before any CPI is issued, so the transfer is never attempted. Hoard, recipient, Position, aggregate and replay all byte-identical.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: a wallet payout against an unresolved Market
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The Core Market is walked back to Phase::Open with its terminal receipt removed -- through the bank, so the alteration actually reaches the chain -- and the same request that just committed is refused Identity (0x5002) at 15,670 CU. The Core state's address is derived from an identity that does not move, so this is a PHASE refusal and not an address one.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with the owner named but not signing
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The owner is named in the request and present in the frame WITHOUT its signature. The SignedDeltaV3 frame spec's SIGNER pin at coordinate 0 refuses first, 0x5201 at 103,634 CU, before any economics is read. Naming an owner is not authorizing anything.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with a signer who is not the Position owner
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A valid signature from an identity that is not request.owner. Coordinate 0 must BE the owner under role Claims, so this refuses Accounts (0x5001) at 8,212 CU -- the cheapest refusal in the set, before the aggregate is even decoded.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with a stranger claiming to own this Position
bindings.note: HOSTILE, the same substitution pushed one step further: the stranger signs AND is named as the owner, so the authority check passes. The evaluator's Position join then refuses Economic (0x5005) at 59,869 CU because the offered account's header says the actor owns it. Behind that stands signed_delta_v3::build_candidates, which would refuse the same frame again on the canonical PDA under (aggregate, stranger) -- two independent derivations of one fact, and the first one is enough.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with another party's Position at this Market
bindings.note: HOSTILE, the same join from the other direction: a Claims capability Position at this same Market, canonical for ITS owner, offered with the wallet's signature. Economic (0x5005) at 59,870 CU. A wallet cannot redeem the representation layer's collateral by pointing at it.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with role Claims with a foreign caller program
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Role Claims means THIS program is the executor and there is no external caller, so coordinates 14/15 are pinned to the Claims program and its ProgramData. A frame naming the test caller there leaves an unauthenticated executable in a role slot; refused Release (0x5202) at 105,911 CU.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: wallet payout with role Trading with an owner signature at the authority coordinate
bindings.note: HOSTILE, the crossing in the other direction and the sharpest one in the set: an EXTERNAL role offering a wallet signature where its own release-pinned caller PDA belongs. Refused Release (0x5202) at 223,065 CU. The owner-signature proof is admissible under role Claims and nowhere else; the two authority kinds do not substitute for one another.
